title: How do we complete a figure with two blue lines?
description: Six figures each have a red part and two blue lines that cross. The red part is flipped over one blue line, and then the whole result is flipped over the other.
teaching_notes: One idea: flip the red part over the first blue line, then flip everything over the second, so both lines become folds. Watch for students who flip the red part over each line separately and forget to flip the new copy.

source: Copy the following drawing on squared paper. Complete each one of them so that the resulting figure has the two blue lines as lines of symmetry.
video_script.why: The child completes a figure around two crossing blue lines by flipping the red part over one line and then flipping the whole result over the other.
video_script.substitution: Flip the red part over the first blue line, then flip the old part and the new part together over the second blue line.
video_script.anchor: Six figures on squared paper, each with a red part and two crossing blue lines: two with slanted blue lines and four with one vertical and one horizontal blue line
video_script.payoff_line: Flip over one blue line, then flip everything over the other.

final_answer.value: mirror the red part in the first blue line, then mirror the whole result in the second blue line; both blue lines are then lines of symmetry
final_answer.spoken: mirror the red part in the first blue line, then mirror the whole result in the second blue line, and both blue lines are then lines of symmetry

hold_back: mirror the red part in the first blue line
never_show: the finished figures before the answer beat
maths_rules: A line of symmetry is a fold line along which one half covers the other exactly.
Flipping the red part over the first blue line gives one matching copy.
Flipping the red part and its copy over the second blue line gives four parts in all.
The finished figure is symmetric about both blue lines.
The first figure, with the red segment near the bottom between two slanted blue lines, completes to a square.
Check: fold along each blue line and see that the halves cover each other.
video_script.design: One idea: flip over one line, then flip everything over the other. Assumes the child can mirror a shape across a single line. The six figures stay on the board from the hook to the end.
open_questions: The six figures are described in words by the worklist and could not be seen, so only the method is taught and only the first figure's result, a square, is named.
